turns.prompt: polish the video board layer. we should move the slots for pickup/dropoff into the system boxes for tiles/palette/dac. remove the enemies on the layer, this layer should just be a race against time. we should have a frame timer box that counts down, and it resets the bits one is carrying  when at zero. should make the pickup systems bigger, and more visual. the tiles box should show the tile currently there for pickup. then take 3 pixels of that. the palette should actually show the palette, and light up the 3 palette entries for the pixels.
turns.reply:
I've reworked the video board (layer -2) as you described, and it's in [fischerq/ludumdare60#61](https://github.com/fischerq/ludumdare60/pull/61). I checked it with a scripted run that teleported the player through two full deliveries: both scored, with no console errors. Nobody has played it with real swipes yet, and I haven't tested the timer running out.

- **No enemies.** The ghost sprites and the sound chip's deadly area are gone.
- **Frame timer box.** It counts down from 12 seconds, and the bar turns red near the end. At zero it shows "DROP", clears whatever you're carrying and fetches a new tile. The timer also restarts after every delivery.
- **TILES box** is big and you walk into it. It shows a real tile from the current picture, enlarged so each board cell holds 2x2 of its pixels. I made it pick a tile with as many colors as possible. Three pixels blink, and you take one by stepping on it.
- **PALETTE box** shows the palette as 8 large swatches, which are the 8 most common colors on screen. The entries for the 3 pixels you're carrying light up, and stepping on one turns that pixel into its color.
- **DAC box:** walk in with all 3 pixels colored to score a goal. It then shows the colors as red/green/blue bars. You still need 4 deliveries to clear the layer.

**Choices I made that you didn't specify:**
- You have to step on each lit palette swatch; just entering the palette box isn't enough.
- The timer is 12 seconds. It's one number in `src/config.js` (`frameTime`) if it feels too tight or too loose.
- I removed the sprite and sound chip boxes and kept VRAM as a decorative box.

**To test on the phone:** go down to layer -2, collect the 3 blinking pixels, step on the lit swatches, then walk into the DAC. Also let the timer run out once while you're carrying pixels, to see whether 12 seconds feels right.

The design doc (`design/systems/layer-deep.md`) is updated, with a new line in its decision log. I also gave the screenshot tool a `--data` option so it can shoot a specific deep layer.

Plan usage at the start of the turn was 2% of the 5-hour limit and 24% of the weekly limit.

turns.prompt: when delivering in the DAC, we should show how the pixels are dropped there, then sent out over a wire
turns.reply:
When you deliver in the DAC, the 3 colored pixels now drop from you into three slots in the box. Bars showing each pixel's red, green and blue levels rise over the slots. Then the pixels leave one after another through the DAC's right side and travel along the video-out wire off the board. I checked it with a scripted delivery and screenshots partway through. The animation played in that order and the goal counted.

The whole thing takes about 2.5 seconds. The four timings are one-line edits in `DEEP.signals` in `src/config.js`. To make room, I extended the wire to the board's right edge. The design doc has the new behavior and a line in its decision log.

**To test on the phone:** deliver once in the DAC and watch the pixels drop in, show their levels, and run out along the wire to the right. Tell me if it feels too slow or too fast.

It's pushed to the same PR: [fischerq/ludumdare60#61](https://github.com/fischerq/ludumdare60/pull/61).
